5.1a — The Axe: Item Pickups & Inventory Bools

Coins and potions changed numbers. The axe changes what you are: it flips a boolean, swaps your animation variant, and suddenly you look like someone who can break down a door. Today: inventory as true/false flags — the cheapest data structure that can possibly work.

Predict First ~10 min

Look at the shipped Player prefab in Assets/Prefabs: it uses the PlayerAnimator with Axe/Shovel variants — the art for axe-wielding already exists. And in PlayerController, find the animation branch from 1.6a that runs on mouse click (Attack trigger). The starter is aching to hand you an axe.

Predict: where should "has an axe" live? A new int field? A list of items? A bool? Argue for your answer in one sentence before reading on — the starter's design uses a bool (hasAxe), because one item, one yes/no, is the honest data structure. Six items would be six bools; sixty would be a list (see the card jam in 10.2a — that is the list era).

Socratic

The AP exam loves questions that ask what data type fits the job. Why is a bool the right abstraction for "has an axe" but the WRONG one for "how many coins"? What does "right size the data" mean — one sentence.

Build Lab ~25 min

Step 1 — the field. In PlayerController, add the pickup family's newest member:

// Inventory
private bool hasAxe = false;

Step 2 — the pickup. The AxeItem prefab exists in Assets/Prefabs: check its collider (trigger) and its tag (Axe? add it if missing — same ritual as 2.3a). Grow OnTriggerEnter2D with a third branch:

if (other.CompareTag("Axe"))
{
    hasAxe = true;
    // swap to the axe animation variant:
    // set the animator's parameter for the axe layer/variant here
    Destroy(other.gameObject);
}

Notice what this branch does NOT do: it touches no StatManager, prints no count. Not every pickup is a number. The axe is capability: a boolean that future code will read before allowing an action. You are building a permission.

Step 3 — see the permission. Prove hasAxe is real state: add a temporary print in Update —

Debug.Log("hasAxe: " + hasAxe);

Run, watch it spam false, pick up the axe, watch it spam true. Delete the print after; the proof is in the behavior.

Step 4 — the art swap. Open the Player's Animator: the axe variant states exist but nothing transitions INTO them. Add an Animator bool parameter (axePickedUp, say), a transition from the normal set to the axe set on "true", and set it from your pickup branch — the same code-sets-parameter, animator-plays-frames split from 1.6a, now driving an equipment change. When it works, your little sprite stops being a tourist.

Bug Hunt: The phantom axe

  1. Set hasAxe = true as the field's starting value. What does the game grant you before you ever found it — and what did the default-after-pickup design protect against?
  2. Pick up the axe, die on a spike (death loop from 2.2a), and watch your back. Do you still have the axe? Should you — and whose decision is that, code or designer?
  3. Add a SECOND axe to the map. Pick up both. What does hasAxe become after the second one — and why is "true" the only correct answer even though the count is two?
  4. You swap the animator parameter name to "hasAxe" in code but the Animator still says "axePickedUp". What is the symptom — silence, an error, or nothing?
Tinker ~10 min

Tinker: Inventory design

  1. Add a shovel sibling (the art variant exists!). Two bools, two tags, two branches — at what number of items does copy-pasting branches become the wrong design?
  2. Design the HUD: how would the player SEE that they hold an axe? Argue sprite-only vs a UI icon — and which does the art variant already give you for free?
  3. Hard: one-use axe — breaking the door consumes it (hasAxe = false, swap back). Which script flips the bool back, and why must it NOT be the pickup branch?

Checkpoint — before moving on, you must be able to:

  • Explain inventory bools vs counters and when each fits
  • Build an item that grants capability instead of a number
  • Drive an animation-variant swap from code through an Animator parameter
  • Trace hasAxe across death (does it persist? should it?)
